rb-0001.title: Use project money helpers for rounding
rb-0001.description: Monetary results must be rounded with the repository's own round_money helper, not Python's round() or bare Decimal.quantize().
rb-0001.content: Python's round() and Decimal.quantize() default to banker's rounding, which produces wrong invoice totals. Always import and call ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent) on any computed money value before returning it.

rb-0002.title: Inspect existing module conventions before implementing
rb-0002.description: Reading sibling functions in the target file reveals required helpers and patterns like to_money, ZERO, and round_money.
rb-0002.content: Before writing a new function, read the surrounding module (e.g. line_total, invoice_total) to see how money is normalized and rounded. Mirror those conventions so the new function is consistent and passes hidden tests.

rb-0003.title: Handle empty collections with the project's zero constant
rb-0003.description: For aggregate functions over possibly-empty lists, return the module's ZERO constant rather than a literal 0 or Decimal(0).
rb-0003.content: Guard against division by zero by checking total quantity first and returning ZERO. Use sum(..., ZERO) as the start value so the accumulator stays a Decimal and matches project style.

rb-0004.title: Mirror existing error codes and validation order from sibling functions
rb-0004.description: Reuse the codebase's established BillingError codes and state-check-first pattern rather than inventing new ones.
rb-0004.content: Before implementing a new function, grep the repo for existing BillingError codes (e.g. invalid_state, non_positive_amount) and copy the same message format and check ordering used by analogous functions like issue_invoice/authorize. This keeps behavior consistent and satisfies hidden tests that assert on error codes.

rb-0005.title: Guard bool when validating integer inputs in Python
rb-0005.description: isinstance(True, int) is True, so explicitly reject bools before the int check.
rb-0005.content: When a parameter must be a positive integer, write `if isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int) or x <= 0: raise ...` — otherwise True/False silently pass as 1/0 and hidden tests for invalid quantity will fail.

rb-0006.title: Normalize money via round_money before range checks
rb-0006.description: Convert unit_price with the project's round_money helper, then compare against ZERO, so string/float inputs and rounding are handled uniformly.
rb-0006.content: Accept flexible price inputs by calling round_money(unit_price) first, then validate `price < ZERO` and store the rounded Decimal on the LineItem. This matches how line_total and authorize handle amounts and avoids type errors on raw strings/floats.

rb-0007.title: Reuse existing period arithmetic helpers
rb-0007.description: When implementing a new time-based function, look for an existing sibling function doing similar period math and mirror its structure.
rb-0007.content: Before writing renewal/period logic, grep for related functions (e.g. current_period) and reuse their exact pattern: normalize inputs with ensure_utc, compute length = timedelta(days=period_days), and use floor division (at - start) // length. This keeps semantics consistent and avoids off-by-one bugs.

rb-0008.title: Handle before-start edge case explicitly
rb-0008.description: For 'first X strictly after t' queries, special-case t before the anchor point instead of relying on floor division.
rb-0008.content: When after < start, floor division yields a negative n and the formula can return the start itself or a wrong value. Return start + length directly for that branch, then use n = (after - start) // length + 1 for the normal case to guarantee strict inequality.

rb-0009.title: Normalize datetimes via the project's ensure_utc
rb-0009.description: Use the repository's existing ensure_utc helper rather than ad-hoc tzinfo checks so naive/invalid inputs raise the project's BillingError.
rb-0009.content: Inspect clock.py/errors.py early; calling ensure_utc on both the query time and stored timestamps gives consistent UTC comparison and correct error codes for naive datetimes, matching hidden-test expectations.

rb-0010.title: Check idempotency key before any validation or mutation
rb-0010.description: When implementing money-moving operations, look up the idempotency key in the audit log first and return the original result early, before state checks or side effects.
rb-0010.content: Team convention requires an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` on every balance-changing operation. Scan `audit.events(<event_name>)` for a matching key and return the original record immediately; only then validate state and apply changes. Always include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write.

rb-0011.title: Enforce approval thresholds as optional keyword-only params
rb-0011.description: Amounts above a policy threshold need a second approver; accept `approved_by=None` so existing callers keep working and raise BillingError when missing.
rb-0011.content: For refunds/credits above 500.00 (finance policy FIN-2026-03), raise `BillingError("approval_required")` if `approved_by` is None; amounts at or below the threshold need no approval. Keep the threshold as a module constant and record `approved_by` in the audit entry.

rb-0012.title: Mirror sibling module patterns for errors, money, and audit
rb-0012.description: Before writing a new function, read adjacent modules (payments.py, money.py, errors.py, audit.py) and reuse their helpers and error codes for consistency.
rb-0012.content: Use `round_money`/`ZERO` from money, `ensure_utc` from clock, and `BillingError(code, detail)` with codes like `invalid_state`, `non_positive_amount`. Validate state (e.g. status must be 'captured'), reject non-positive amounts, and cap cumulative refunds at the captured amount before mutating `refunded_amount`/`status`.

rb-0013.title: Reuse existing money helpers for rounding and zero
rb-0013.description: When implementing monetary functions, import and use the repo's existing round_money and ZERO constants rather than ad-hoc round() calls.
rb-0013.content: Inspect sibling modules (e.g. payments.py) to find shared helpers like round_money and ZERO, then apply them consistently so rounding and comparisons match the rest of the codebase.

rb-0014.title: Match existing error-raising conventions
rb-0014.description: Follow the established pattern of raising BillingError with a snake_case code and stringified value for invalid inputs.
rb-0014.content: Grep for existing BillingError usages to learn the code/argument style (e.g. BillingError("non_positive_amount", str(amount))) and mirror it for new validation, such as invalid_rate.

rb-0015.title: Normalize numeric inputs via Decimal(str(x))
rb-0015.description: Convert non-Decimal numeric inputs with Decimal(str(value)) to avoid float artifacts, and catch InvalidOperation to raise a domain error.
rb-0015.content: Accept both Decimal and plain numbers by wrapping non-Decimal values in Decimal(str(x)); catch InvalidOperation and re-raise as the project's error type with from None to keep tracebacks clean.

rb-0016.title: Check for repo-wide conventions before implementing a new operation
rb-0016.description: The first attempt was rejected because it missed a team convention (idempotency_key) that applied to all money-moving operations, not just the one being added.
rb-0016.content: Before writing a new payment/credit/invoice operation, grep the repo for existing conventions like idempotency_key, audit event patterns, and keyword-only params, and check for docs/CHANGELOG notes about incidents. Apply cross-cutting conventions even when the issue text doesn't mention them.

rb-0017.title: Implement idempotency by checking audit events first
rb-0017.description: Idempotent operations must look up prior audit entries by key before validating state or mutating anything.
rb-0017.content: Add `*, idempotency_key=None` to the signature, then first scan audit.events(<event_type>) for a matching idempotency_key and return the original result if found. Only after that do state validation and mutation, and include idempotency_key in the audit.record call.

rb-0018.title: Mirror sibling functions for state transitions and audit
rb-0018.description: Following the existing authorize/invoice patterns (BillingError invalid_state, ensure_utc, audit.record naming) produced a consistent implementation.
rb-0018.content: When adding a state-transition function, copy the structure of an existing sibling: raise BillingError('invalid_state', ...) with the current status, normalize times with ensure_utc, and record an audit event named <entity>_<action> with the relevant fields.
